summary: Review round applied on the same branch: all eight R-25 findings fixed at the source and covered by tests, plus one extra guard found while proving them. (1) coerce_scope no longer infers a scope from the words inside it - an out-of-vocabulary scope goes only to its category's deterministic fallback (project -> gotchas, global -> environment), because the scope decides which roles receive the note. (2) The repair CLI now rich.markup.escape()s every interpolated scope/note/reason/path and prints the skipped-row reason after a colon instead of in [brackets], which Rich parsed as a style tag and dropped. (3) --dry-run only ever says 'would move / would re-render / would collect / would remove' and names each dead file once; --no-gc moves rows and re-renders but deletes nothing. (4) The GC predicate is now four-part and visible (in_layout_dir AND not canonical_file AND unowned AND _renderer_output), so hand-authored markdown indexed via 'memory import --markdown' is never deleted. (5) update() validates a throwaway preview BEFORE assigning, so a refused PATCH leaves the row and its rendered file unchanged without relying on a rollback. (6) _file_for is reverted to main's body and reachable_roles resolves through the same rule (role, else scope, through ROLE_MEMORY_KEY): a legacy role='logbook-writer' row keeps its own dead file and is REPORTED as uninjectable instead of re-homed - no role-injection or rendering semantics changed. (7) docs/memory.md now separates the rejecting boundaries (POST, PATCH, 'memory add') from the repairing ones (import JSON, import --markdown, fix-scopes) and the coercing/dropping one (a Worker suggestion). (8) Evidence is split into per-file COMPLETE diffs with a DIFF_COMPLETE trailer plus a sha256 manifest, because the combined diff supplied last round was truncated inside memory_service.update(). While writing test 8 a real gap surfaced: importing an export whose legacy row is still stored under its dead scope added a SECOND copy under the fallback scope (and rendered the line twice); the duplicate check now takes both spellings (_import_keys). Counts: make test 520 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed, make lint clean, 49 T-4 tests pass, all offline, no API keys, no network. Final state verified at branch tip 95f3c78: make test 520 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed, make lint clean, tree clean.

contracts_touched: Memory entry schema (memory_entries + MemoryCreate/MemorySuggestion): columns and JSON fields unchanged; only validation, coercion and reporting were added. No migration.

REST API shapes under /api: POST /api/memory and PATCH /api/memory/{id} now return the already-frozen {"error", "detail"} 400 body for an out-of-vocabulary scope. No field added, removed or renamed; no new route.
Build-log events: added the event names memory_scope_substituted and memory_suggestion_dropped (additive per the contract; no rename or removal). The line shape is unchanged.

CLI command surface: added 'orchestrator memory fix-scopes' (authorised by DoD 3) and the additive options --dry-run/--gc-only/--no-gc on it and --uninjectable on 'memory list'. Existing commands keep their arguments and exit codes.

Artifact/rendering contract 'approved entries render to $ORCHESTRATOR_HOME/memory/**.md with one "- <content>  <!-- mem:ID -->" line each': _file_for and render_file are main's code, so rendering is unchanged. fix-scopes rewrites the `scope` column only, re-renders both files, and collects a rendered ghost that has no owning entry (authorised by DoD 3) under a predicate that cannot match hand-authored markdown. 'Existing memory_entries rows must not be deleted; scope repair is idempotent' holds: fix_scopes never deletes a row and a second run moves nothing (test_fix_scopes_moves_legacy_rows_and_re_renders_both_files).
Path-independent verification commands: consumed, not modified. make test / make lint still route through scripts/orch_verify.sh and every evidence log carries its ORCH_VERIFY| marker line.

Out of scope and untouched: which scopes each role receives (ROLE_PROJECT_SCOPES), for_prompt, ROLE_MEMORY_KEY, the GUI Memory page, docs/frozen-contracts.md, core/models.py, core/schemas.py, core/state.py, and every migration.
assumptions: DoD 1 names only the project fallback (gotchas). Global suggestions are handled symmetrically with the constant FALLBACK_SCOPE[global] = 'environment'; role suggestions have no fallback and are dropped, as DoD 1 requires. Both are asserted by tests and stated in docs/memory.md.

DoD 4 says role entries are resolved 'through _file_for/ROLE_MEMORY_KEY', so the inj marker judges a role row by the file it renders into. A legacy row with an EMPTY role column and a valid scope therefore reads 'ok' even though for_prompt selects role memory on the role column and would not inject it. That asymmetry is main's, is documented in docs/memory.md ('Role-aware injection'), cannot be created by any boundary any more (_validate fills role from scope), and is deliberately NOT auto-repaired because DoD 3 covers invalid SCOPES and MemoryUpdate has no role field (adding one would change the frozen MemoryCreate/MemorySuggestion/PATCH shape). It is reported in the fix-scopes skip reason so an operator sees it.

The repair path is idempotent per the frozen task contract, so importing an export twice never duplicates a fact; this round also made the FIRST import safe against the still-unrepaired row (memory_service._import_keys :821), which was the only behaviour change I added beyond the reviewer's findings.

Evidence logs in verify-evidence/T-4 are stamped at HEAD 5c678f9 with tree=0 dirty entries outside that directory; make test and make lint were then re-run at the branch tip 95f3c78 (after the evidence commit) on a clean tree with the identical result: 520 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed and 'All checks passed!'. The per-file diffs in verify-evidence/T-4/diff_*.txt are computed against the merge-base db00112 at 5c678f9, i.e. every source and test change on this branch; the tip commit only adds evidence text.

R-25 provenance (finding 9) is explained, not papered over: runs/25/run.json records exit_code=0, timed_out=False, cancelled=False, status=completed, handoff_arrival=clean_exit and no error, so the trailing 'harness reported an error while exiting 0' is a mislabel produced by run_service.exit_state_text (:390-405, unchanged since the merge-base db00112), whose final else fires for any zero exit. Nothing on this branch writes or reads that wording.

It is one line ('else "harness reported an error while exiting 0"' with no result.error condition), but the string is already archived inside historical run.json artifacts, so a fix changes operator-facing wording of past runs. DoD 3 says 'orchestrator memory fix-scopes, or repair during import'. Both are implemented. If the reviewer prefers exactly one repair surface, say which and I will drop the other (import_all's coercion, or the CLI command).
The GUI Memory page still shows no uninjectable indicator; the task calls that a follow-up. Confirm it should be a separate task rather than folded in.

memory_suggestions.content: coding-orchestrator memory scopes are a CLOSED vocabulary checked by membership, not shape: memory_service.GLOBAL_SCOPES (environment|preferences|patterns), PROJECT_SCOPES (conventions|decisions|gotchas), ROLE_SCOPES (== ROLE_FILES: architect|worker|supervisor, after ROLE_MEMORY_KEY aliases reviewer->architect, agent->worker). A row stored outside its own category's vocabulary is rendered to a file no injector ever reads. Out-of-vocabulary scopes are coerced to the deterministic fallback (project->gotchas, global->environment) and NEVER inferred from words inside the scope, because the scope decides which roles receive the note. Repair with `orchestrator memory fix-scopes [--dry-run|--no-gc|--gc-only]`; audit with `orchestrator memory list --uninjectable`.

In this repo any Rich console.print that interpolates operator data (a scope, a branch name, a reason string) MUST pass it through rich.markup.escape first. `console.print(f"... [{why}]")` silently DELETED the whole reason from `memory fix-scopes` output in R-25: Rich parsed the brackets as a style tag and the operator got a line with the explanation missing. Escape the data, keep markup only in the literal part of the string, and write a test that puts a bracketed value through the CLI.

Anything that deletes files under $ORCHESTRATOR_HOME/memory must use a renderer-shaped predicate, not 'unowned means dead': docs/memory.md tells operators to hand-write lines there and index them with `memory import --markdown`. The rule shipped in T-4 is in_layout_dir AND not canonical_file AND unowned AND _renderer_output (first line exactly '# <stem>', every other non-blank line '- ...  <!-- mem:N -->').
